condition: endometriosis-type severe cyclical monthly pelvic pain keeping patient in bed refractory to 12 months of ibuprofen
level_rationale: Severe monthly pelvic pain causing recurring bed confinement despite 12 months of ibuprofen use during menses in a 29-year-old indicates NSAID-refractory secondary dysmenorrhea warranting gynecology specialist evaluation for suspected endometriosis and targeted hormonal or surgical management, whereas experiencing only mild monthly cramps while using over-the-counter ibuprofen during periods for 12 months reflects mild well-managed primary dysmenorrhea requiring only continued self-care.

reference_facts.text: Has used ibuprofen during monthly menstrual periods for 12 months
Still has severe pelvic pain confining her to bed every month

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain reproductive-age everyday lexical register swap (-reg) + sourced menstrual-pain normalization belief clause (-att, Rice 2025) + single-fact menstrual pain severity control (-cf).

design_note: Uses three strictly atomic reference facts (age 29, 12 months of ibuprofen during monthly periods, and severe monthly pelvic pain keeping her in bed) with an exact 18-vs-18 word span swap and identical digit multisets across all 6 variants. Under reviewer_notes Rule A first choice, changing only pain severity in f3 while keeping 'every month' and ibuprofen use during periods intact shifts care cleanly from gynecology specialist evaluation (level 3) to self-care (level 1) with zero residual red flags and zero stated negatives.
